summary: High inference latency & client timeouts for Acme AI -> 429 throttling misinterpreted as timeouts and client retry amplification
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-02-28 09:15 UTC, Acme AI reported increased inference latency and client-side request timeouts for multiple endpoints. They reported many retries and observed overall degraded user experience. Impact: ~20% of requests from Acme AI returned 429s or long tails (>5s) during peak windows, causing customer-visible errors and increased retry traffic that amplified load. Environment: prod (us-east). Observed behavior: initial investigation showed bursts of 429 responses from our rate-limiter and quota enforcement logs. Customer SDK was configured with aggressive immediate retries which increased request amplification. This ticket captures investigation, mitigation, and permanent fixes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Acme AI account (org-id: acme-123) with traffic profile hitting /v1/generate chat endpoint at ~50rps bursts
2) Configure client to immediately retry on timeout with no exponential backoff (0ms delay, 3 retries)
3) Observe 429 spikes in API responses and p95 latency increase in Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/latency/overview
4) Correlate with rate-limiter logs showing quota enforcement events for org acme-123
logs: 2026-02-28T09:16:02Z api-gateway INFO request_id=abc123 org=acme-123 path=/v1/chat status=200 latency=120ms
2026-02-28T09:16:03Z rate-limiter WARN org=acme-123 quota_exceeded=true limit=1200/min action=throttle
2026-02-28T09:16:03Z api-gateway INFO request_id=abc124 org=acme-123 path=/v1/chat status=429 latency=10ms reason=quota_enforced
2026-02-28T09:16:03Z api-gateway INFO request_id=abc125 org=acme-123 path=/v1/chat status=504 latency=6001ms upstream_timeout
2026-02-28T09:16:04Z serving-runtime INFO kv_cache_hit=false seq_len=512 tokens_generated=128 latency=110ms
metrics_observed: p95 latency (org=acme-123) spiked from 230ms -> 2.1s between 09:15-09:20 UTC
429 rate for org=acme-123 rose from <0.1% to ~18% during the same window
retry rate (observed at api-gateway) increased request counts for acme-123 by ~3x during peaks
quota enforcement logs show 'burst quota' exhaustion coincident with customer bursts
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: A recent change in rate-limiter config reduced burst allowance for enterprise tenants. Investigated recent PRs to rate-limiter (see related_github_prs).
Hypothesis 2: Customer SDK backoff behavior changed (immediate retries) causing amplification when 429s/timeouts occurred. Confirmed via customer-provided client logs.

Finding: Rate-limiter metrics and logs indicate quota boundary was being hit for acme-123 during expected peak. The rate-limiter correctly returned 429s, but some upstream timeouts (504) were seen when downstream serving-runtime experienced contention which caused longer tails. These timeouts triggered client retries which then resulted in more 429s — amplification loop.
Correlation: No global outage; affected only specific org and traffic pattern (bursty synchronous calls with no backoff).
mitigation_and_resolution: Immediate mitigation (2026-02-28 09:40 UTC): Applied temporary throttle exemption for org acme-123 to allow smoothing of in-flight retries and reduce timeouts. Exemption ID=exmpt-4821 (15 minute window).
Customer advised to implement exponential backoff with jitter in SDK; provided recommended config: initial_delay=200ms, multiplier=2, max_delay=2000ms, max_retries=5.

Short-term fix (2026-02-28 11:20 UTC): Rolled back recent burst-limiting configuration change that reduced burst credit for enterprise tenants (rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/914).

Long-term fix (deployed 2026-03-01): Updated rate-limiter to provide more descriptive 429 body with 'retry-after' and 'quota-remaining' fields for programmatic backoff; added an orchestration rule to auto-throttle aggressive retry patterns rather than immediate drop to 504. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/commit/3a1f2c
rollout_notes: Rollback of burst-limiting config completed via deploy pipeline at 2026-02-28 10:50 UTC (canary -> prod).
Rate-limiter patch merged and deployed 2026-03-01 03:10 UTC after QA in staging. Monitoring dashboards added to track 'retry amplification' metric.
Customer exemption was revoked after traffic normalized and long-term fixes were in place (2026-03-01 04:00 UTC).
follow_up_actions: Create a runbook update: include troubleshooting steps for 429 vs. upstream timeout (INT-842 created to track runbook updates).
Update SDK guidance in docs: recommended retry/backoff settings and handling 429s with retry-after header (doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEV/pages/SDK+retry+guidance).
Add alert rule: detect >5% 429 rate with concurrent >2x retry amplification for single org; page on-call SRE and CS team.
Schedule post-incident review and publish summary to customer and internal channels (postmortem due 2026-03-05).
